battle.name: 格謙起義
battle.brief: 隋大業九年（613年）四月，百濟王弟格謙糾集都城貴族在泗沱起兵，兵鋒直指王城與宮門；中央宿衛將領龜愫、辛邑集兵平叛，兩名主謀被擒後獲赦，流放邊州。卡面的亞述長弓並未隨軍而至，但百濟弓兵沿用的角筋複合短弓，正是同一條技術路線的東亞分支，兩者在弓兵主導的城防與車陣裡佔同一位置。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 格謙起義是隋大業九年（613年）百濟都城泗沱（今韓國忠清南道扶餘一帶）的一次宮廷政變，捲入的三方是百濟王族與都城貴族、百濟中央的平叛將領，以及正在半島上用兵的隋朝。叛方的骨幹是王弟格謙與從弟禮，加上在都城握有兵甲與私兵的氏族首領，史家以「不逞之徒」形容這批追隨者；他們以宗室身分在宮城內部發動，意圖廢黜義慈王另立新君，行動集中在王城、宮門與城門這幾個控制城防的要點。平叛方是百濟的中央武力：龜愫與辛邑執掌都城宿衛與兵甲，叛事一起便能集結城內部隊，靠王城垣、門樓與城內街坊的防衛把叛軍壓回去。百濟的國家架構是王都、諸都、州郡三層，《隋書·東夷傳》載其設五都，泗沱為王都所在，其餘都城與州郡分據漢江、洛江下游，掌兵的則是各城鎮的守將與將帥，兵農合一，平日為地方武備，戰時隨王命集結。外部壓力來自隋朝：隋煬帝在大業九年正進行第二次征討高句麗，連年下令百濟出兵助陣並交納糧秣，隋使與被送作人質的百濟宗室常駐都城。北方高句麗與東方倭國則各自在等百濟露出破綻，好乘勢牟利。
countriesEn: The Geon rising was a palace coup fought in the Baekje capital of Sabi, in what is now the Buyeo area of Chungcheongnam-do, in the ninth year of the Sui's Daye era, 613 CE. Three parties were drawn into it: the Baekje royal house and the aristocracy of the capital, the Baekje central commanders who put the rising down, and the Sui dynasty, which was at the time campaigning on the peninsula. The backbone of the rebel side was the king's younger brother Geon and his cousin Li, joined by clan heads in the capital who held arms and private soldiers of their own; historians describe the followers they gathered as unruly and disaffected men. Acting on the strength of their blood relation to the king, they struck inside the city, and their intention was to depose King Uija and set up a new ruler; their operations were concentrated on the royal castle, the palace gates and the city gates, the points that control the defence of a walled town. The side that suppressed them was the central armed strength of Baekje: Gwissu and Sin-eup held the night watch and the armoury of the capital, and as soon as the rising began they were able to bring the troops inside the walls together, and it was the wall of the royal castle, the gate towers and the streets of the city that kept the rebels from spreading. The structure of the Baekje state ran in three tiers, the royal capital, the other capitals, and the commanderies: the Sui Shu records in its account of the eastern peoples that Baekje had five capitals, with Sabi as the seat of the king, while the remaining capitals and commanderies lay along the lower Han and the lower Rok. The troops were distributed among the city garrisons and their commanders; soldier and farmer were the same man, a local levy in time of peace and a mustered force in time of war. The external pressure came from the Sui. Emperor Yang was in the midst of his second campaign against Goguryeo in 613, and had ordered Baekje again and again to send troops to help and to deliver grain, while Sui envoys and members of the Baekje royal house held at the capital as hostages sat in the city permanently. Goguryeo in the north and the Japanese court in the east were each waiting for a crack to appear in Baekje, so that they might profit by it.
people: 這場政變裡的關鍵人物大半集中在百濟王族。義慈王在位期間（599年至632年）百濟正處於最險的位置：向北與高句麗爭地，向南要應付隋朝的連續徵召，向內則要安撫王族的爭端。他的母親華義夫人寵愛親子瓊，一度使原定的太子扶餘被廢，扶餘隨後被送往隋廷作人質，這段廢立留下的怨恨，是日後宗室分裂的源頭。叛方領袖格謙是義慈的弟弟，從弟禮亦屬近支，兩人都有資格在王族中主張位置，卻長期被排除在權力核心之外；史書記他們起事時糾集的是都城的不逞之徒與若干武人，行動限於宮城與城門一帶，準備有限。平叛方的主角則是龜愫與辛邑兩名將領：二人執掌都城宿衛，得到王城與宮門的控制權，叛軍才沒有機會擴散到城外，也無法號召州郡。義慈王本人在事平之後展現出罕見的克制，對格謙等人先行赦免、再流放邊州，這種不殺的處理在當時的東亞王朝並不尋常。隋朝那一邊，煬帝正是藉著百濟內亂重新加緊對百濟的索取；《北史》於同一時代另記一則年代相近的刺讎事：沙磧真之父為百濟人所殺，她隨兄入隋京，在館舍中刺殺仇人而得隋廷褒獎，年十七。這則旁記說明那幾年百濟與隋之間的關係緊張到催生私人報復。
peopleEn: The people who matter in this coup are gathered, for the most part, inside the Baekje royal house. During the reign of King Uija (599 to 632) Baekje stood in the most dangerous position of its history: it contested ground with Goguryeo to the north, it had to answer the repeated summons of the Sui to the south, and inside the court it had to settle the quarrels of the royal clan. The king's mother, Lady Hwaui, favoured her own son Qiong, and the crown prince Buyeo was set aside and afterwards sent to the Sui court as a hostage; the resentment left over from that reversal of the succession is the source of the split in the clan that would come later. The leaders of the rebel side, Geon and Li, were the king's brother and a close kinsman; both had the standing to make a claim within the royal house and both had long been kept out of the centre of power. The records say that the men they gathered were disaffected inhabitants of the capital together with a number of soldiers, and that their action was confined to the palace quarter and the city gates, with limited preparation. The central figures on the side that put the rising down were the two commanders Gwissu and Sin-eup. They held the night watch of the capital, and it was their seizure of the royal castle and the palace gates that kept the rebels from spreading outside the walls or from calling up the commanderies. King Uija himself showed rare restraint after the affair was over: he pardoned Geon and the others first and then exiled them to the border provinces, and such a refusal to kill was not ordinary in the East Asian states of the time. On the Sui side, Emperor Yang used the disturbance in Baekje to tighten his demands on Baekje once more. The Bei Shi, writing of the same decades, also records a vendetta of a slightly later date: the father of Shaqizhen was killed by a man of Baekje, and she came to the Sui capital with her brothers, killed her father's murderer in the lodgings of the embassy, and was rewarded by the Sui court; she was seventeen. The sidelight shows how strained the relations between Baekje and the Sui had become, strained enough to breed private revenge.
kits: 卡面這把亞述長弓並沒有出現在泗沱的城頭。亞述長弓是公元前八世紀前後亞述帝國的標準武器：以木為胎、內裡貼角、外層纏筋的複合結構，弓梢反曲，短而有力，亞述軍靠弓兵在戰車兩側掩護、車兵在弓兵掩護下推進的組合，一步步征服兩河流域；但它與百濟的弓隔了一千三百多年，也隔了半個地球，兩者並非同一件武器。把它放進這場起義的裝備表，是因為它代表弓在人類戰爭中的第一個大規模樣本：把拉力與箭速壓進一副可重複使用的短弓身裡，再用車陣與箭雨去兌換戰果。百濟弓兵用的正是這條技術路線的東亞版本，即角、筋、木複合的短弓，結構原理與亞述弓同源，形製則更小、更適合在城牆上連射；百濟還大量使用弩，弩是守城與野戰近程壓制的骨幹。步兵的長兵器是槊與矛，配置木盾；防護以皮甲為主，鐵札甲見於貴族與軍將，扶餘一帶百濟墓葬出土的鐵甲片、長矛與骨鐵箭鏃，可以與《北史》的記載互相對照。馬匹多自高句麗與北方輸入，車以牛車為主，攻城備雲梯、撞車與飛石，糧食以稻米、粟與鹽為大宗，漢江與木津江的水路是運糧的幹道。同一時期的隋軍則以玄甲精騎、投石機與浮橋這些新技術著稱，《資治通鑑》記大業九年隋軍進攻平壤，在城下築土山、於浿水架浮橋，正是那一年東亞攻城技術的水準。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card never stood on the walls of Sabi. The Assyrian bow was the standard weapon of the Assyrian empire around the eighth century BC: a composite structure of a wooden core lined with horn on the inside and wrapped with sinew on the outside, with recurved tips, short and powerful. The Assyrian army advanced on the two riverlands by a system in which archers covered the flanks of the war chariots and the chariot crews pushed forward under that cover. But this bow and the bow of Baekje are more than thirteen centuries apart, and half a world of geography apart; they are not the same weapon. It belongs in the equipment table of this rising because it stands for the first large-scale model of the bow in the history of war: the pull and the speed of the arrow compressed into a short bow that can be used again and again, and the result then cashed in through chariot formations and showers of arrows. What the Baekje archers used was the East Asian version of that same line of technique, the short composite bow of horn, sinew and wood, whose structural principle is of a piece with the Assyrian bow, only smaller in form and better suited to shooting repeatedly from a parapet. Baekje also used the crossbow in quantity, and the crossbow was the backbone of close-range suppression in siege and in the field. The long weapons of the foot were the spear and the long spear, with wooden shields; protection was chiefly leather, with iron lamellar armour for the aristocracy and the commanders, and the plates of iron armour, the spears and the bone and iron arrowheads excavated from Baekje tombs around Buyeo can be checked against what the Bei Shi says. Horses came in large part from Goguryeo and the north, carts were ox carts, the siege train included scaling ladders, battering rams and stone throwers, and grain was chiefly rice, millet and salt, with the waterways of the Han and the Mucheon as the arteries of supply. The Sui army of the same years was famous for new techniques, the armoured elite cavalry called xuanjia, stone-throwers and floating bridges; the Zi Zhi Tong Jian records that in the ninth year of Daye the Sui army before Pyongyang raised earthen mounds against the walls and spanned the Bei river with a floating bridge, which is the standard of Eastern Asian siegecraft in that very year.
tactics: 起義本身的打法，從有限的記載與常理推知即可，必須說明：留下這段文字的史書只寫了結果，沒有留下戰況，因此以下分為「書中有據」與「據常理推想」兩層。書中有據的是：叛軍發動於都城內部，捲入的是宮城、王城與城門一帶的武人與氏族首領；平叛由龜愫、辛邑以中央宿衛承擔；事後兩名主謀被擒獲並遭赦免流放。由推想補出的部分，是城防體制本身的樣子：泗沱的都城垣與宮區基址今日仍可見於扶餘一帶，牆頂可容弓兵列陣，弓手以連射壓制接近城下的人馬，弩手集中於門道與城樓射界，弓弩之間形成遠近兩層；叛軍若奪門成功便可引外兵入城，因此平叛的第一個動作應是封閉城門、切斷街道、把交戰限制在宮城周邊的狹窄地帶，再以甲士結陣逐段清剿，而不是讓戰線拉長到州郡。任何內亂都靠糧秣說話：泗沱一城之食需靠漢江水路與周邊州郡的賦稅維持，一旦叛軍能截斷城內外的往來，守城方反而會先動搖，這正是平叛方堅持速戰速決的理由。
tacticsEn: How the rising was actually fought has to be reasoned out, and it has to be said plainly that the historians who wrote it down recorded the outcome and not the fighting; what follows is therefore divided into two layers, what the books actually attest and what follows from the general shape of things. What is attested is this: the rising was launched inside the capital, the men involved were soldiers and clan heads from the palace quarter, the royal castle and the city gates; the suppression was carried by the central night watch under Gwissu and Sin-eup; and afterwards the two principal men were taken and then pardoned and exiled. What has to be supplied by inference is the shape of the defensive system itself. The circuit of the royal city of Sabi and the foundations of the palace quarter can still be seen in the Buyeo area today; the wall walk would have taken a line of archers, who kept up a steady shooting rate against everything that came up under the wall, while the crossbowmen were concentrated on the gate passages and the gate towers, so that bow and crossbow formed two layers, far and near. Had the rebels taken a gate they could have brought foreign troops in through it, so the first act of the loyal side must have been to close the gates, cut the streets and hold the fighting inside the narrow ground around the palace quarter, and then to clear it section by section with shielded infantry in ranks, rather than let the front stretch out into the commanderies. Every civil war is decided by supply. A city such as Sabi drew its food from the river route of the Han and from the taxes of the surrounding commanderies; if the rebels could cut movement between the city and the country, the defenders would be the first to waver, and that is exactly why the loyal commanders insisted on ending it quickly.
data: 可核對的數字不多，先列有據的。時間是隋大業九年，即公元613年，叛事繫於四月，兩名主謀被流放至邊州。規模方面，《資治通鑑》記隋軍第二次征高句麗時出軍「百餘萬」，所仰給的糧秣須自河南、江南、蜀地運下，書中以百萬石一類的概數寫之；百濟方面也曾奉隋命出兵助戰，兵數以萬計，但具體名冊不傳。百濟都城泗沱在《隋書·東夷傳》中與其餘四都並列，該書曾記百濟的疆域與戶口，但數字出自古代史家的概說，不宜細究；王城垣周長以公里計，宮區與坊里分隔清楚，今日扶餘一帶的百濟王都城址仍可辨認。考古方面，忠清南道與忠清北道一帶的百濟墓葬，從五世紀末到七世紀初的封土中出土了大量隨葬品，包括鐵甲片、鐵矛、馬具上的鐙與轡、骨製與鐵製箭鏃，以及公孫金鼎一類帶銘文的青銅禮器；其中武寧王陵等大墓的隨葬品以千計，可見一個養得起數量可觀的兵員與馬匹的國家。人口與總兵力沒有留下數字，只能從五都的分置、州郡的設置與墓葬的等級推知其組織規模，實際作戰兵力則完全無從核算。《北史》所記沙磧真刺讎一事，只留下她「年十七」一條年齡數字，沒有留下其他可核對的細節。
dataEn: There are not many figures here that can be checked, so let the attested ones come first. The date is the ninth year of Daye, 613 CE; the rising is tied to the fourth month; and the two principal men were exiled to the border provinces. On scale, the Zi Zhi Tong Jian records that in the Sui's second campaign against Goguryeo the army set out 'over a hundred thousand' strong, and that the grain it depended on had to be brought down from Henan, from Jiangnan and from Shu, written in the book in round figures of a million shi; Baekje also sent troops to assist the Sui at the Sui's command, numbering thousands, but no muster survives. The capital of Sabi is listed in the Sui Shu's account of the eastern peoples together with four other capitals, and the same book gives figures for the extent of the country and for the number of households, but these come from the generalisations of ancient historiographers and should not be pressed; the circuit of the royal city wall runs to kilometres, and the palace quarter is clearly separated from the wards, and the site of the Baekje royal capital can still be recognised in the Buyeo area today. In archaeology, the Baekje tombs in Chungcheongnam-do and Chungcheongbuk-do have given up large assemblages from burial mounds of the late fifth to the early seventh century, among them plates of iron armour, iron spears, the stirrups and bits of harness, bone and iron arrowheads, and inscribed bronze ritual vessels of the kind of the Gongsun golden ding; in the great tombs, that of King Muryeong among them, the grave goods are counted in thousands, which shows a state rich enough to maintain a considerable number of men and horses. No figure for population or for total strength survives; the size of the organisation can only be inferred from the distribution of the five capitals, the setting up of the commanderies and the grading of the tombs, while the actual field strength cannot be reckoned at all. For the vendetta of Shaqizhen recorded in the Bei Shi, the only number preserved is her age, seventeen; nothing else checkable was left behind.
cause: 起義的成因有三層。最外一層是隋朝：從大業八年起，隋廷在第一次征討高句麗失利之後，轉而把百濟當作後勤與兵源的索取對象，屢次下令出兵助陣、交納糧秣，隋使與質於京師的百濟宗室長期滯留都城。國勢的壓力並不只落在邊境上，它直接擠壓了王室的財政與榮譽，也讓都城的氏族首領得以藉「抗隋」為名聚兵。中間一層是王室的繼承糾葛：義慈王的母親華義夫人力挺親子瓊，廢太子扶餘而令其為質於隋，宗室之中因此分成兩撥；有資格、有企圖、卻沒有位置的王子，正格謙與禮這類人物。內裡一層則是百濟自己的政治結構：五都分置，兵權分散在各城鎮與氏族手中，都城宿衛雖有龜愫、辛邑這樣能打的將領，但整個統治仍靠少數人與家族之間的默契維持。一旦宮城之內出現兩套旗號，忠誠就會按照親疏而非按道理分邊，叛亂才能以如此小的力量在首都掀起。也因此，起義其實是百濟在隋朝壓力之下，把內部矛盾集中到首都的一次爆發，而不是一次有明確軍事計劃的戰爭。
causeEn: The causes of the rising lie in three layers. The outermost is the Sui. After the failure of the first campaign against Goguryeo in the eighth year of Daye, the Sui court turned Baekje into a source of logistics and of men, ordering it again and again to send troops and deliver grain, while Sui envoys and Baekje princes held as hostages in the capital remained there for years. The strain of the state did not fall only on the frontier; it pressed directly on the finances and the prestige of the royal house, and it gave the clan heads of the capital a cover for mustering men under the name of resistance to the Sui. The middle layer is the tangle of the succession. Lady Hwaui, the king's mother, pushed her own son Qiong, the crown prince Buyeo was set aside and sent to the Sui as a hostage, and the royal house was divided into two camps accordingly; the princes who had standing, who had designs, and who had no place were precisely men of the kind of Geon and Li. The innermost layer is the political structure of Baekje itself. With five capitals, military authority was dispersed among the city garrisons and the clans, and although the capital's night watch had such competent commanders as Gwissu and Sin-eup, the whole government still rested on understandings between a few men and their families. Once two sets of banners appeared inside the palace quarter, loyalty divided by kinship and not by reason, and a rising of this kind could raise a very small force in a capital. The rising was therefore less a war conducted to a military plan than a concentration, brought about by the pressure of the Sui, of Baekje's internal contradictions in its own capital.
impact: 這場起義的直接結果是一次政權的加固，但長遠的影響寫在別處。第一，義慈王靠龜愫、辛邑平亂，卻在赦免與流放之間展現出另一種思路：不以殺戮固結人心，讓王族分支彼此牽制；此後扶餘於632年義慈去世後在北方即位，是為武王，639年顯宗承之，百濟王統由此維繫到唐初。第二，隋朝把百濟的內亂讀成軟弱的證據，隨後在615年前後直接出兵進攻百濟，百濟告急於高句麗與倭國，東方半島從此捲入隋、唐、倭三方糾纏，最終在663年白村江一線，百濟與高句麗聯軍及倭國援軍面對唐軍而全線崩潰。第三，就軍事技術而言，這一年是東亞弓兵與攻城技術的分水嶺：隋軍在平壤城下築土山、架浮橋、造飛石，百濟則仍以城牆弓弩與木柵守禦；兩種樣式此後在半島上長期並行。第四，史料層面的影響更為實際：關於百濟早期王室的記載幾乎全靠《北史·百濟傳》這一段文字，它既是這場起義唯一的一手記載，也讓後世無法知道起義的具體戰況、兵力與折損，只能靠制度與考古去補。
impactEn: The immediate result of the rising was a reinforcement of the government, but the long consequences lie elsewhere. First, King Uija put the rising down with the help of Gwissu and Sin-eup, and in the choice between killing and banishing he showed a different way of thinking: not to cement his position with blood, but to let the branches of the royal house hold one another in check. Buyeo then took the throne in the north in 632, after King Uija died, as King Mu, and King Seonjong succeeded him in 639, and the Baekje royal line thus held on until the early Tang. Second, the Sui read the disturbance in Baekje as proof of weakness and within a few years moved troops against the kingdom itself, around 615; Baekje appealed to Goguryeo and to the Japanese court for help, and the eastern peninsula was from then on caught in the tangle of Sui, Tang and Japan, until in 663, on the line of the Baekgang river, the allied armies of Baekje and Goguryeo together with the Japanese auxiliaries collapsed before a Tang force. Third, as a matter of military technique, this year was a watershed for archery and siegecraft in East Asia: the Sui raised earthen mounds, spanned rivers with floating bridges and built stone throwers before Pyongyang, while Baekje still defended itself with wall archers, crossbows and wooden palisades, and the two styles ran side by side on the peninsula for a long time afterwards. Fourth, the effect on the historical record is more practical still. Everything we know about the early Baekje royal house rests on this single passage in the Bei Shi, the account of Baekje; it is at once the only primary source for this rising and the reason that later generations cannot know the actual fighting, the numbers engaged or the losses, and must fall back on institutions and on archaeology to fill the gap.
result: 613年四月，格謙與禮在泗沱起事，兵鋒直指王城與宮門。龜愫、辛邑以中央宿衛接管城防，封閉城門、分割街坊，把叛軍限制在都城一角，兩名主謀被擒；整場衝突沒有演成百濟與高句麗之間的戰爭，也沒有變成州郡連兵，兵禍止於首都一隅，這是它與同期其他叛亂最大的不同。事後義慈王不誅而赦，把格謙與禮流放邊州，這種寬大在東亞王朝的記載裡並不多見，一般被視為義慈仁懦、缺乏狠厲之處；龜愫與辛邑則因平亂之功受信，王城宿衛的權重此後更集中於中央。對外而言，百濟的處境反而惡化：隋朝自此認定百濟可欺，數年後便移師東來，屢次遣使索取貢賦並出兵攻擊；百濟不得不向高句麗與倭國求援，把自己的存亡綁在別人的善意上。史書留下的一條記錄到此為止：起事的時間、參與者、平叛的將領與最後的處分俱全，而起義的實際規模、交戰的細節以及雙方折損的數目一概不傳，後人只能從泗沱城的城防格局與百濟墓葬中出土的甲冑與箭鏃，去想像這座城在那一年的樣子。
resultEn: In the fourth month of 613, Geon and Li rose in Sabi, and the point of their thrust was the royal castle and the palace gates. Gwissu and Sin-eup took over the defence of the capital with the central night watch, closed the gates, cut the streets into sections and shut the rebels into one quarter of the city; the two leaders were taken. The whole affair did not develop into a war between Baekje and Goguryeo, and it did not turn into a general rising of the commanderies; the violence stayed inside one corner of the capital, and that is what distinguishes it most sharply from other revolts of the same period. Afterwards King Uija did not kill but pardoned, and exiled Geon and Li to the border provinces. Such leniency is not common in the East Asian dynastic record, and it is generally read as evidence that Uija was indulgent and lacked hardness; Gwissu and Sin-eup, meanwhile, were trusted for the work of putting the rising down, and the weight of the royal capital's night watch became more concentrated in the centre than before. From abroad, Baekje's position grew worse rather than better. The Sui concluded from the rising that Baekje could be pressed, and within a few years moved east, sending envoys to demand tribute and tribute goods and then to attack; Baekje had to ask Goguryeo and the Japanese court for help, tying its own survival to the goodwill of others. The record in the books ends there. The time of the rising, those who took part, the commanders who suppressed it and the final sentence are all preserved; the actual scale of the rising, the detail of the fighting and the numbers lost on either side are preserved nowhere, and later generations can only look at the defensive layout of Sabi and at the harness and arrowheads dug out of Baekje tombs, and try to imagine what that city was like in that year.
